correctness.rationale: The specified 80-vertex finite incidence graph is exhaustively generated. For incident/nonincident point–line pairs, (C2,C3,C4) chain counts are (18,81,120)/(28,87,72) and the integral Smith ranks of (d3,d4) are (18,63)/(28,50), every nonzero invariant equal to one. Both boundary compositions vanish. All 59 Smith invariants of [d4|nine explicit cycles] equal one, certifying an integral basis of local rank nine. Symplectic transvections, explicitly checked to be graph automorphisms, transitively permute all 160 incident and 1440 nonincident point–line ordered pairs, and chain reversal supplies the opposite orientation. Bipartite parity eliminates same-part endpoints. The global rank is 2*1440*9=25920. The packaged checker was executed successfully from its exact source path.

The closest specific second-off-diagonal result is mod-two magnitude homology for the order-two Tutte–Coxeter quadrangle, not the order-three integral homology or the nine-element cycle basis. An endpoint-localized projective-plane computation studies girth six and bidegree (3,4), and generalized-quadrangle Vietoris–Rips results use a different invariant. Actual claim/alias/parameter searches disclosed no result implying this integral classification. A full-text inspection of the closest order-two item was unavailable; undocumented or unindexed equivalents remain possible.

value.rationale: This identifies the exact integral second-off-diagonal magnitude group of the canonical 80-vertex symplectic generalized-quadrangle incidence graph. Nine geometrically indexed octagon cycles per nonincident antiflag form an integral basis, strengthening finite-field ranks to a torsion-free integral classification and making the geometrical support of the classes reproducible. It is a natural next-valency benchmark precisely at the sharp girth-eight boundary, not an arbitrary graph slicing or a marginal numerical refinement.
